questions.question: Which heading is for the main title of the page?
options: <h6>, because it is the last heading tag.
questions.explanation: <h1> is used for main headings. There is no h0 or heading element.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.question: How many heading levels does HTML give you?
options: One: h, with a level attribute.
Unlimited <h> tags with a size attribute.
questions.explanation: HTML has six levels of headings, h1 through h6.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.question: What is <h2> for?
options: The document title in the tab.
A CSS class that makes text large.
questions.explanation: <h2> is used for subheadings. Further sections use h3 and so on.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.question: Which snippet is a paragraph?
questions.explanation: A paragraph is the p element. There is no text or para tag.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.code: A paragraph is a block of text.

questions.question: Which list numbers its items?
questions.explanation: Ordered lists are numbered. ul is bullets. dl is terms and definitions.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Ordered lists are lists where each item in the list is numbered.

questions.question: Which list uses bullet points?
questions.explanation: Unordered lists begin with a bullet point rather than characters that indicate order.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Unordered lists are lists that begin with a bullet point

questions.question: What does a definition list contain?
options: A set of terms and the definitions for those terms.
questions.explanation: Definition lists are made up of a set of terms along with the definitions for each of those terms.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Definition lists are made up of a set of terms along with the definitions for each of those terms.

questions.question: Which child belongs inside <ul>?
options: <ul> as a required wrapper around each word.
questions.explanation: List items are li elements. Not item, not a bare paragraph as the only child.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: each item in the list is numbered

questions.question: Why not pick <h6> just to make text small?
options: Heading level is the outline. Size is CSS.
h6 is only allowed in tables.
questions.explanation: Browsers display headings at different sizes, but you pick the level for structure. CSS later controls size.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Browsers display the contents of headings at different sizes.

questions.question: Which markup nests a list correctly?
questions.explanation: A nested list lives inside an li of the parent list, not as a sibling of li.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: Unordered lists are lists that begin with a bullet point

questions.question: A recipe's steps should be marked as?
options: <dl>, because each step is a definition.
questions.explanation: A set of steps for a recipe that must be performed in order is the book's example of an ordered list.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: the list might be a set of steps for a recipe that must be performed in order

questions.question: Which heading sequence matches a page with one title and two sections?
questions.explanation: One h1 for the page. Each section is an h2. Do not skip to invent a look.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: If there are further sections under the subheadings then the <h3> element is used, and so on

questions.question: Which is a definition list pair?
questions.explanation: dt is the term. dd is the definition. They sit in a dl.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: a set of terms along with the definitions for each of those terms

questions.question: What happens if you skip from <h1> to <h4> for looks?
options: The outline lies. Use h2, then CSS for size.
The browser invents h2 and h3 for you.
HTML forbids h4 after h1, so the page will not load.
questions.explanation: Levels are structure. Duckett notes browsers size headings, and CSS is how you control that later.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett
reference.excerpt: You will see how to control the size of text, its color, and the fonts used when we come to look at CSS.

questions.question: Which copy should be a paragraph, not a heading?
options: A two-sentence introduction under the title.
A label for a group of links in a table of contents.
questions.explanation: Headings label sections. Running copy is p.

reference.book: HTML and CSS: Design and Build Websites by Jon Duckett

questions.question: Write heading(level, text) that returns <hN>text</hN> for level 1–6.
questions.explanation: h1–h6 are the six heading levels. The number is the outline depth.
